findings: Missed scene links (test inputs only, each checked by eye on contact sheets in sheets/ and frames/): shared object vocabulary (idf-weighted, >= 2 distinctive names) links 0007-0009 (pier/boat lake), 0010-0014 (farm house, cart, bird), 0015/0019 with the 0016/0017 atrium, 0045-0050 (photo-lab street), 0187-0191 (truck warehouse), 0193-0195 (Jupiter model), 0202-0209 (typewriter desk), 0210-0222 (cat room); segmented-frame NCC .966 links 0038_seg~0043_seg (beach rock); an eye-verified identical prior links 0030 to 0029 (same beach rock, sea and eagle). 148 vocabulary candidates were rejected by eye (colour-car/streetlight/door names across different scenes). Identical prior text alone is not enough (two such pairs are different scenes).
simulation_0030's depth_info is copied from simulation_0140 (neon-sign building; same bird distances 25.328/24.899 m and a neon-sign entry absent from the beach scene).

T on the new links: 17 D3 rows take stated values (boat 3.62/0.75 m, bird 1.19 m, person 1.87/1.75/1.8 m, bicycle wheel 0.65 m, eagle 0.8 m). Validation answers on the test copy of simulation_0009 equal the transferred values exactly (1044: 3.62, 1046: 0.75; measurement only).

K (clip scale) is camera-specific: a family-level K from other clips' facts gives no gain in LOFO (.767 -> .767). A single other-object fact gives only +.013 (.769 -> .782, 112 pairs) and K from the boat facts hurts 5 of 7 known 0009 rows (pier, cabin floor, steps are not under-scaled), so clip K was NOT extended to new single-fact clips. Same-object facts carry the scale strongly (pairs .414 -> .614; size->size boat pairs .55 -> .85): Claude's model of one object has the right shape but the wrong size -> KOBJ.

P on the extended families: LOFO on all 90 D3 facts KP .906 (raw .766); on the 19 new-link facts KP .742 vs raw .674; old facts unchanged (.951 -> .949). A spread guard hurts: high-spread groups gain the most from pooling (pool .83 vs own .53), so none is used; min_bases 2 ~ 3, kept 3 as in probe 5.

Implausible direct scale: simulation_0032_segmented (segmented basketball clip, no context) has direct person 15.7 m, ball 2.45 m, throw 25 m/s; geometry from its own depth_info measures 1.76 m, 0.278 m, 2.64 m/s, and rescaling the direct answers by a human height (1.8/15.7) independently gives 0.28 m and 2.9 m/s. No other D3 sim clip has this pattern.

Lab (313 untouched rows): no principled family lever left. Lab statics are calibrated rig geometry (props already pooled by probe 5; books differ between events, persons have no stated sizes, slopes/tables already pooled). Lab motion is the open question (GT 1.2-1.6x physical in 0034a/0054a/0061 but physical in slope/floor scenes); probe 6 tests lab motion -> direct, so nothing is stacked here. Slope physics (v = a(t - t0), v_end = sqrt(2aL)) agrees with direct, not geometry, in 0001/0002/0024, but that is the same lab-motion routing question. Only one new lab fact: the 0018 tennis ball (stated 6.7 cm in S3 priors; LABFACT only ran on props asked in >= 2 events).
